annotationRationale: The essential step is decomposing a rounded solid into pieces associated with the box's faces, edges, and corners. Rectangular-prism surface area and the exact prism, cylinder, and sphere volume formulas then determine the coefficients. Both supplied references use this same geometric route.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Geometry is correct; no repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: Independently, the volume is (4π/3)r³+8πr²+38r+12, giving bc/(ad)=19, choice B. The question and key agree, including at r=0. No figure is required.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: Both supplied references use the same geometric decomposition. No additional distinct accessible method is needed.
review.annotationCheck: cnm_h107 appropriately assesses decomposition into basic solids. Prism volume, surface area, cylinder volume, and sphere volume are correctly supporting concepts; the contextual role is empty.
review.areaCheck: Geometry is correct; no repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Coordinate clamping minimizes squared distance separately in each direction and justifies the exhaustive face, edge, and corner partition. The six slabs contribute 38r; the twelve quarter-cylinders have total length 32 and contribute 8πr²; eight spherical eighths contribute (4π/3)r³. Together with volume 12, these give 19.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Accurately identifies the shared LIVE and AoPS decomposition as third-party-informed work. The nearest-point justification and explanatory prose are independently developed; shared formulas and solid types are mathematically necessary.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The opening explains why decomposition fits. The coordinate argument justifies completeness and non-overlap, and the fractional cylinder and sphere counts are explained. The argument works for every r≥0 without a diagram.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: All five immediate IDs match the written derivation: cnm_h107 for decomposition and counting pieces, cnm_p163 for prism volumes, cnm_p161 for face areas, cnm_p207 for cylinders, and math:sphere-volume for the numerical sphere formula.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The supplied exact native links for composite solids, prism volume, prism surface area, and cylinder volume are appropriate. math:sphere-volume has no accepted CN link; this is an honest alignment gap.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: Prism calculations support components of 5.MD.C.5, 5.MD.C.5b, and 7.G.B.6; cylinder and sphere calculations support components of 8.G.C.9 and G-GMD.A.3. The remaining partial or narrower links involve packing, fractional lengths, nets, contextual modeling, or formula derivations that this solution does not demonstrate. No full-standard coverage is implied.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: The assessed/support distinction is appropriate, and the exact sphere-volume node correctly supplies the constant that a radius-scaling topic would not provide.
